title: THEIR NAMES, THEIR LANDS, THEIR GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These were the chiefs descended from Esau, by name, according to their clans and regions: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, Magdiel and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land they occupied. This was Esau, the father of the Edomites." - Gen 36:40-43 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes as it began — with a roll call of Esau's chiefs, now listed by their clans and the regions they settled. "This was Esau, the father of the Edomites." A single man's line had become a network of clans spread across the land, each with its leaders and its territory. From the brother who lost the blessing came a substantial, established people.

It is worth remembering that this whole chapter is devoted to a nation outside the covenant line. Why does God's Word give so much space to Edom? Partly to remind us that God's care and attention are not confined to one people. He watches over all the nations of the earth; every people group falls under His sovereign gaze (Acts 17:26).

Edom's later story would be a mixed and often troubled one — at times a bitter enemy of Israel. Yet even so, God called the Edomites Israel's "brothers" (Deut 23:7). Nations, like families, carry both blessing and brokenness through their history, and all of it unfolds under God's watchful rule.

This points us toward the wideness of God's heart. From the very beginning He intended blessing to reach "all peoples on earth" (Gen 12:3), a promise fulfilled in Christ, in whom people of every nation are welcomed (Gal 3:8; Rev 7:9). The God who carefully recorded Edom's chiefs is the God who calls people from every land into His family. His salvation is for the nations.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I share God's heart for all the peoples of the earth?
2. How does it move me that God's blessing in Christ is for every nation?
3. Where can I reflect God's wide welcome to those different from me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, Your care reaches every nation, and Your salvation in Christ is for all peoples. Give me Your heart for the world, and help me to welcome others as You have welcomed me. Amen.
